issues.title: [TODO] Make maxSpaceCount responsive to dashboard layout
issues.description: The SpacesOverviewCard hardcodes `maxSpaceCount = 4`, displaying exactly 4 spaces regardless of available viewport space. This should be made responsive to utilize available dashboard space on larger screens (6+ spaces on desktop, 2-3 on tablet, 1-2 on mobile).
issues.body:
## Summary

The `SpacesOverviewCard` component currently displays a fixed number of spaces (`maxSpaceCount = 4`). On larger desktop screens with the dashboard grid layout, this wastes available space; on mobile, 4 spaces may be too many. The `maxSpaceCount` should be calculated dynamically based on the container width and the expected viewport, providing better use of screen real estate across all breakpoints.

## Source Location

**File:** [`components/dashboard/SpacesOverviewCard.server.tsx`](https://github.com/cckssr/NextLaBIS/blob/develop/nextapp/src/components/dashboard/SpacesOverviewCard.server.tsx#L6)
**Line:** 6-9

## Current Code Context

```typescript
/**
 * Props for SpacesOverviewCard component.
 *
 * TODO: maxSpaceCount should be calculated based on window size of the Dashboard
 * @param maxSpaceCount - Maximum number of spaces to display in the card.
 */
interface SpacesCardProps {
  maxSpaceCount?: number;  // Hardcoded default in component: maxSpaceCount = 4
  spaces: SpaceDisplayData[];
}

export function SpacesOverviewCard({
  maxSpaceCount = 4,  // <-- Hardcoded default
  spaces,
}: SpacesCardProps) {
  return (
    <Card withBorder={true} p="lg" shadow="md" radius="lg">
      {/* ... */}
      <Stack align="stretch" justify="flex-start" gap="md" mt="md">
        {spaces.slice(0, maxSpaceCount).map((space) => (
          <SpaceCard key={space.code} {...space} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

**Dashboard Layout Context:**

```typescript
// From src/app/(misc)/dashboard/page.tsx (inferred)
// Dashboard uses Mantine Grid with responsive breakpoints:
// - base (mobile): full width
// - sm (tablet): 50%
// - lg (desktop): multi-column layouts
```

## Analysis

**Current Limitation:**
- `maxSpaceCount = 4` is a static default; no responsiveness
- On desktop with wide viewport, the card could display 6-8 spaces and utilize space better
- On mobile, 4 tall SpaceCard items create excessive vertical scroll
- Parent dashboard layout already uses Mantine responsive Grid; component should follow suit

**Why This Matters:**
- **UX**: Mobile users see fewer relevant spaces before scrolling; desktop users don't see enough
- **Space Utilization**: Dashboard grid layout adapts to viewport; this card should too
- **Consistency**: Other dashboard cards (ActivitiesCard, etc.) should follow the same pattern
- **Scalability**: If users have 100+ spaces, hardcoded 4 items becomes insufficient

**Implementation Approach:**

Since this is a **Server Component**, we cannot use `useMediaQuery` hooks. Instead:

1. **Move calculation to parent (Dashboard page):**
   - Dashboard page receives viewport info via CSS or layout props
   - Calculate `maxSpaceCount` at the page level and pass it down
   - Pro: Centralized responsive logic; Con: Adds prop drilling

2. **Use CSS-based approach (Mantine Grid):**
   - Render SpaceCards inside a Mantine `Grid`/`GridCol` instead of a Stack
   - Let CSS handle the layout; show all spaces and let CSS hide overflow
   - Pro: Truly responsive; Con: Changes component structure

3. **Use Mantine Container + Stack responsive props:**
   - Keep Stack but add responsive `gap` and conditional rendering logic
   - Example: `const displayCount = isWideScreen ? 6 : isTablet ? 3 : 2`
   - Pro: Works in Server Components; Con: Requires parent context

**Recommended**: Option 2 or 3 - prefer CSS-based responsive handling over prop drilling.

## Suggested Implementation

**Option A: Responsive Grid Layout (Recommended)**

```typescript
import { Card, Group, Text, Title, Grid, GridCol } from "@mantine/core";

export function SpacesOverviewCard({ spaces }: SpacesCardProps) {
  return (
    <Card withBorder={true} p="lg" shadow="md" radius="lg">
      <Group gap="md" align="center" mb="xs">
        <IconFolder size={20} />
        <Title order={4}>Your Spaces</Title>
      </Group>
      <Text c="dimmed">Overview of your spaces with recent activity</Text>
      <Grid mt="md" gutter="md">
        {spaces.map((space) => (
          <GridCol key={space.code} span={{ base: 12, sm: 6, md: 4, lg: 3 }}>
            <SpaceCard space={space} />
          </GridCol>
        ))}
      </Grid>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

This uses Mantine's responsive Grid system:
- `base: 12` - Full width on mobile (1 column)
- `sm: 6` - Half width on small screens (2 columns)
- `md: 4` - Third width on medium (3 columns)
- `lg: 3` - Quarter width on large (4 columns)

Grid automatically arranges items; no hardcoded `maxSpaceCount` needed.

**Option B: Calculate from parent props (if Grid is unsuitable)**

```typescript
interface SpacesCardProps {
  spaces: SpaceDisplayData[];
  containerWidth?: "full" | "half" | "third"; // Passed from dashboard layout
}

export function SpacesOverviewCard({ spaces, containerWidth = "half" }: SpacesCardProps) {
  const maxSpaceCount = {
    full: 8,
    half: 4,
    third: 2,
  }[containerWidth];
  
  return (
    <Stack>
      {spaces.slice(0, maxSpaceCount).map((space) => (
        <SpaceCard key={space.code} space={space} />
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Component responds to viewport width (mobile: 1-2, tablet: 3-4, desktop: 6+ spaces)
- [ ] No hardcoded `maxSpaceCount = 4` default
- [ ] Uses Mantine breakpoints (base, sm, md, lg)
- [ ] Passes mobile, tablet, and desktop viewport testing
- [ ] ESLint and TypeScript checks pass
- [ ] Works as Server Component (no `"use client"` needed for responsiveness)
- [ ] TODO comment updated with issue number

## Phase Alignment

**Phase 0 Enhancement** - Improves visual design and UX during mock-data driven development. No API changes required.

## Priority

Low - Quality of life improvement; not blocking other features

## Related Issues

- See SpaceCard issue (#XXX) for related type refactoring
- Dashboard layout patterns should be consistent across all cards

---

issues.title: [TODO] Add RichTextEditor for HTML editing in edit mode
issues.description: The MultilineRenderer currently uses a plain Textarea for editing, but in view mode it renders HTML content. This creates a mismatch: users cannot edit the formatting they see. In Phase 1, the edit mode should use @mantine/tiptap's RichTextEditor to provide WYSIWYG editing that matches the rendered output.
issues.body: ## Summary The `MultilineRenderer` has a fundamental edit/view mode mismatch: - **View Mode**: Renders HTML content (bold, italic, links, lists, etc.) using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` - **Edit Mode**: Uses a plain `Textarea` (plain text only, no formatting) This creates a poor user experience: users see rich formatting but cannot edit it; when they edit and save, all formatting is lost. In Phase 1, the edit mode should use **`@mantine/tiptap` RichTextEditor** (Mantine's TipTap integration) to provide WYSIWYG editing. ## Source Location **File:** [`components/masterdata/MultilineRenderer.tsx`](https://github.com/cckssr/NextLaBIS/blob/develop/nextapp/src/components/masterdata/MultilineRenderer.tsx#L36) **Line:** 36 ## Current Code Context ```typescript /** * Renderer for MULTILINE_VARCHAR property type. * View: Renders sanitized HTML content or plain text. * Edit: Textarea for plain text editing. * * TODO: Replace Textarea with RichTextEditor (@mantine/tiptap) in Phase 1 * for proper HTML editing support. */ ``` ## Analysis **Current Problems:** 1. **Edit/View Mismatch**: Users see HTML-formatted content but cannot edit formatting - View: `Bold text and links` → Rendered as bold text and clickable links - Edit: User gets plain text editor → All formatting lost on save 2. **Data Loss**: Formatting (bold, italic, links, lists) is visible but uneditable - User sees: "This is **important** documentation" - User edits and sees: plain text "This is **important** documentation" (literal asterisks) - User saves and all formatting is lost 3. **Poor UX**: Users are confused why they can't edit what they see 4. **Type Mismatch**: `MULTILINE_VARCHAR` can contain HTML, but our edit interface only supports plain text **Why RichTextEditor (TipTap):** - **WYSIWYG**: What you edit is what you see (and get) - **Mantine Integration**: `@mantine/tiptap` provides React components with Mantine styling - **HTML Output**: TipTap generates clean HTML; pairs with HTML view mode - **Structured Editing**: Handles complex formatting (nested lists, tables, code blocks) - **Lightweight**: TipTap core is minimal; extend with plugins as needed - **Phase Progression**: Aligns with Phase 1 feature expansion (real content editing) **Implementation Complexity:** - **Low-Complexity Path** (Phase 1 initial): Basic formatting (bold, italic, links, lists) - **Medium-Complexity Path**: Add tables, code blocks, media embeds - **High-Complexity Path**: Custom content types, collaborative editing (Phase 2+) **Phase Alignment:** - **Phase 0**: Keep plain Textarea; HTML view is nice-to-have - **Phase 1**: Switch to RichTextEditor; users need to edit real content - **Timing**: Medium priority in Phase 1; not blocking other work ## Suggested Implementation ### 1. Install @mantine/tiptap ```bash cd nextapp npm install @mantine/tiptap @tabler/icons-react @tiptap/react @tiptap/starter-kit ``` ### 2. Create Rich Text Editor Wrapper Component ### 3. Update MultilineRenderer to use RichTextEditor ### 4. Testing Strategy ```typescript // Test cases: // 1. View mode with HTML → Renders formatting // 2. Edit mode → RichTextEditor shows formatting toolbar // 3. User bolds text → HTML output includes tags // 4. User adds link → HTML output includes tags // 5. Save and reload → Formatting preserved across sessions // 6. Plain text input → No formatting, renders as text ``` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] @mantine/tiptap installed and configured - [ ] RichTextEditor wrapper component created with basic formatting tools (bold, italic, links, lists, headings, code) - [ ] MultilineRenderer edit mode uses RichTextEditor instead of Textarea - [ ] Edit mode generates HTML output that matches view mode - [ ] View mode and edit mode are consistent (WYSIWYG) - [ ] User can edit existing HTML content and formatting is preserved - [ ] Toolbar is accessible and sticky (visible during scrolling) - [ ] Form integration works (onChange updates form state correctly) - [ ] Build passes; no TypeScript errors - [ ] Component still works as Client Component with proper hooks - [ ] TODO comment updated with issue number ## Phase Alignment **Phase 1 (API Integration)** - Medium priority. Needed for users to edit real OpenBIS content with formatting. Not blocking other Phase 1 work. ## Priority Medium - Improves UX for content editing; depends on Phase 1 timeline. ## Related Issues - DOMPurify HTML sanitization (#XXX) - Must be completed before this to ensure safe HTML handling - Type system work (#XXX) - MULTILINE_VARCHAR type handling - Form integration (#XXX) - Ensure form submission works with HTML content --- *This issue was generated from a code comment. Pairs with sanitization work in Phase 1.*
